status_note: Status: review-01 response, 20 October 2026. Original Padova v1 and climate v2 load effects are quarantined after the confirmed hourly state-transition defect. Twenty corrected v3 annual runs provide candidate four-site effects with author arithmetic and full-step checks; scientific interpretation awaits independent review of the local correction. No empirical heating-accuracy claim is made.

GAP-001.exact_claim: The selected respondent's reported mean winter-day system operating hours in three eight-hour bands do not identify unique within-band times. In this model those durations are encoded as hours at a 22°C high setpoint, not as a constraint on actual positive heating-load hours.
GAP-001.assumptions_and_uncertainty: Integer/coarsened reported means are mapped to a repeated two-level 22/19°C thermostat schedule; both contiguity and daily repetition are assumptions. Heating may be delivered at 19°C setback.
GAP-001.counterevidence_alternative_explanation: The survey asks mean system on-hours rather than thermostat levels; the simulation's temperature mapping is a separate assumption and does not reproduce observed burner duty.
GAP-001.permitted_manuscript_wording: Reported mean operating hours leave timing unidentified; our model encodes them as high-setpoint periods while allowing setback heating.

RQ-001.exact_claim: For one illustrative dwelling, one selected Veneto survey response and Padova-coordinate TMY, compare annual useful sensible heating and maximum hourly load under three placements of the same 4/4/1 encoded 22°C high-setpoint hours; a 19°C setback permits heating in other hours.
locators: RQ-FREEZE | 01_plan/research_questions.md primary RQ and fixed-case boundary
RQ-001.assumptions_and_uncertainty: The 4/4/1 encoded high-setpoint hours are fixed; actual positive-load hours and duration are outputs and need not equal 9 h/day. The physical case remains illustrative.
RQ-001.dependencies_next_action_owner: Simulation owner completed corrected Padova run and full-step checks; reviewer 02 must independently inspect local correction and outputs.
RQ-001.permitted_manuscript_wording: We compare three placements of equal encoded high-setpoint periods under one assumed case.

MET-001.exact_claim: Current GRINS EndUse.py converts each reported band duration into one seeded contiguous binary profile segment, then maps binary 1/0 to assumed 22/19°C high/setback setpoints for this timer-selected respondent; positive heating is permitted at the setback setpoint.
locators: ISTAT-Q2013 | questionnaire p43, question 3.13 option _2 timer
DISPATCH-DIAGNOSTIC | 07_reviews/reviewer_01/independent_checks.json positive heat at 19°C in archived outputs; figures quarantined
MET-001.assumptions_and_uncertainty: The source 22/19°C values are not measured respondent setpoints. The binary profile represents the modeled high-setpoint choice, not equipment availability or actual burner runtime.
MET-001.permitted_manuscript_wording: The inspected source places a contiguous high-setpoint segment in each reported time band and allows heating at the lower 19°C setting outside it.

MET-002.exact_claim: The three modeled alternatives preserve the same 4/4/1 encoded daily high-setpoint hours in their respective bands, varying only contiguous placement; they do not preserve the duration of actual heating delivery at either setpoint.
MET-002.assumptions_and_uncertainty: 22°C applies during encoded high periods and 19°C outside within modeled season; ideal heating can run under either setting. Earliest/latest are alternatives, not extrema.
MET-002.permitted_manuscript_wording: The comparison fixes high-setpoint duration within each reported band while changing its placement; actual heating runtime remains free to vary.

MET-003.exact_claim: A bounded local single-commit 1C adapter now uses unchanged EUReCA sensible_balance_1C algebra but evaluates free and constrained candidates from one prior state and commits only one accepted hourly state; this corrects the observed transition defect in the archived adapter without changing external checkouts.
MET-003.assumptions_and_uncertainty: The correction supports only this ideal sensible 1C case with no mechanical/natural ventilation or latent gains; it is not a general EUReCA systems replacement, conference reproduction or empirical calibration.
MET-003.counterevidence_alternative_explanation: Archived v1/v2 recursive dispatcher violated state balance at mode changes; direct pure-network algebra checks did not catch it.
MET-003.dependencies_next_action_owner: Reviewer 02 to independently inspect local correction, transition tests and annual residual checker; external benchmark and measured accuracy remain absent.
MET-003.permitted_manuscript_wording: A local study-specific adapter selects one hourly 1C solution from the same prior state and commits it once; its validity remains under independent review.

RES-003.exact_claim: The corrected Padova v3 seeded, early and late binary profiles each encode 4/4/1 high-setpoint hours in the 05–13, 13–21 and 21–05 bands; this does not constrain positive heating-load hours at the 19°C setback.

RES-003.permitted_manuscript_wording: The corrected run inputs retain the 4/4/1 encoded high-setpoint durations; heating can also occur at setback.

RES-004.label: Corrected Padova candidate outputs

These are candidate model outputs pending independent correction review, not accepted empirical findings.
locators: RUN-PADOVA-V3 | 05_simulations/climate_campaign_v3/Padova/completion_manifest.json frozen hashes and imported EUReCA path
RES-004.assumptions_and_uncertainty: One deterministic assumed case under a TMY. Percent denominator is corrected seeded output. Values remain conditional on adapter correctness and independent review; no population or empirical confidence interval.
RES-004.counterevidence_alternative_explanation: The original v1/v2 annual/peak figures were produced by a dispatcher that failed state balance and are quarantined. Corrected values differ materially, including reversal of annual-effect sign, demonstrating why old values cannot be used.
RES-004.falsification_or_weakening: Independent review finding an incorrect single-commit transition, residual checker, source mapping, or run hash would withdraw the candidate numbers.

new_claims.label: Single-commit correction gate
new_claims.exact_claim: A study-specific local 1C adapter must select off/heating/cooling from candidates evaluated against the same beginning-of-hour state, commit once, and pass explicit mode-transition and every-hour air/surface/mass residual checks before annual outputs are admitted.
new_claims.population_geography_period_comparator_u: One ideal sensible 1C zone, hourly, no mechanical/natural ventilation or latent gains; 1e-6 W numerical residual tolerance.
new_claims.assumptions_and_uncertainty: Adapter uses the unchanged pure EUReCA network solver with bounded local state selection; checker must be independent of engine and use exported old/current states.
new_claims.counterevidence_alternative_explanation: Passing network equations does not verify envelope truth, weather representativeness, software generality or measured accuracy.
new_claims.falsification_or_weakening: Reviewer-discovered state mismatch or checker dependence on incorrect saved states would defeat this gate.
new_claims.dependencies_next_action_owner: Reviewer 02: inspect candidate selection, one-commit behavior and independent full-step checker.
new_claims.permitted_manuscript_wording: The corrected pilot applies a one-state-commit hourly 1C selector and full-step balance checks; independent review remains pending.

new_claims.dependencies_next_action_owner: Simulation owner: preserve archived files and labels; author: never reuse their effect magnitudes as scientific results.
